name: ioquake3
summary: The maintained Quake III Arena engine. It ships its own game logic, so it can host as well as play.
description:
ioquake3 is the community continuation of id's Quake III Arena engine, and it is the engine this build's Quake III path is written against.

Three things about it were established by looking at what upstream actually publishes rather than by assuming:

1. **The game logic ships with the engine.** `Linux.zip` carries `baseq3/vm/qagame.qvm`, `cgame.qvm` and `ui.qvm` beside the two executables, and the macOS bundle carries the same as `.dylib`s. That is why this profile declares all five actions where FTEQW's Quake II profile declares one: a local ioquake3 server needs no third-party gamecode.
2. **What it does not carry is the game.** Upstream's own words: *"The Quake 3 engine is open source. The Quake III: Arena game itself is not free. You must purchase the game to use the data and play Quake 3 with ioquake3."* `pak0.pk3` is id's, it is not ours, and the Companion never downloads, copies or redistributes it.
3. **There is nothing to pin.** ioquake/ioq3 publishes no GitHub release and no tag; the builds are unversioned rolling zips at `files.ioquake3.org`. A signed catalogue entry names a size and a digest, and neither is a property of a URL whose contents change. So this profile is `user_path`, like every other engine profile here.

The executables are named for the architecture upstream builds — `ioquake3.x86_64` and `ioq3ded.x86_64`, with `.exe` on Windows. macOS is the exception: its download is a zip inside a zip holding `ioquake3.app`, whose binaries are plainly `ioquake3` and `ioq3ded`. A profile declares one file name per executable, so on macOS point the Companion at the binary itself — `companion engine bind` takes a path, and the declared name is only what is looked for under an install root.

`fs_homepath` is deliberately not sent. ioquake3 keeps a player's settings, screenshots and demos under their own home directory — `~/.q3a`, `%APPDATA%\Quake3`, `~/Library/Application Support/Quake3` — and a launcher that quietly moved them somewhere else would be a launcher that lost somebody's config. The compiler is the opposite case and does redirect it, because a build must read only what was bound to it.

This profile was written from ioquake3's own published documentation, and two of its lines are now measured rather than read (ioquake3 1.36, Linux, `Q3_011`), in a game folder holding NO id Software data and started with `com_standalone 1`: the dedicated server loads a map out of a PK3 and prints `InitGame:` with the map's name, and prints `Can't find map` — staying up, exiting 0 — for one it does not have; the client loads the world and then stops with `DEFAULT_MODEL (sarge) failed to register`, because Quake III's client game needs the player model in `pak0.pk3`. Nothing here has been run with Quake III's own data: playing Quake III needs a copy of Quake III, which is not ours to have. So `map_loaded` is observed for the dedicated server and is the documented `CL_InitCGame:` line, not an observed one, for the client.

Quake III support in Auto-Pigeon is work in progress. Core editing is available, but shader, patch, entity, compilation and engine workflows may be incomplete, and this profile is part of that path.

license.name: GNU General Public License v2.0 or later
license.notice: Quake III engine source ports are separate programs under their own licences. This profile configures one; it does not contain, link or relicense it. Game data — the PK3 files, maps, textures, sounds and game logic shipped with a commercial release — is not covered by that licence, and the Companion never copies, uploads or redistributes it.

platforms.note: Upstream's Windows.zip carries ioquake3.x86_64.exe and ioq3ded.x86_64.exe; nobody here has run either.
Upstream's Linux.zip carries both binaries. Run here (1.36) with NO id data only: the dedicated server loads a packaged map, the client stops at the missing player model.
Upstream's macOS download holds ioquake3.app, whose binaries are named `ioquake3` and `ioq3ded` without the architecture suffix. Bind the executable by path there.
Upstream's macOS build is Intel; on Apple Silicon it runs under Rosetta 2. The binaries inside the bundle are named as above.
Upstream publishes no arm64 binary; build it from source. Its file name will not be the x86_64 one declared here, so bind the executable by path.

acquisition.title: Use a copy you already have
acquisition.hint: choose the ioquake3 executable — `ioquake3.x86_64` on Linux, `ioquake3.x86_64.exe` on Windows, `ioquake3.app/Contents/MacOS/ioquake3` on macOS
acquisition.note: There is no managed download for any engine here, and for this one there could not be: upstream publishes rolling builds at fixed URLs, with no version and no digest to pin.

content_layouts.title: The base game
content_layouts.note: Where Quake III's own data lives, including the pak0.pk3 you bought. The Companion reads it and never writes to it.

content_layouts.title: A PK3 archive in the base game
content_layouts.note: A PK3 is a zip. Quake III loads every one it finds, in name order, later ones overriding earlier.

content_layouts.title: A mod or project directory
content_layouts.note: A game directory beside baseq3, named by the `fs_game` cvar. This is where the Companion stages the PK3 you built.

actions.title: Play a map
actions.description: Starts the engine and loads one map. `fs_game` is a directory NAME beside baseq3, which is what upstream documents; the path it is found under is `fs_basepath`.

options.name: standalone
options.title: A free standalone game, not Quake III Arena
options.description: Sends `+set com_standalone 1`, ioquake3's own switch for a game that is not Quake III. Measured on ioquake3 1.36: without it the engine stops with `Quake 3 data files are missing` when `pak0.pk3` is absent; with it the engine runs whatever game the `baseq3` directory holds, which still has to carry a non-empty `default.cfg` and that game's own data. It does not make Quake III's data unnecessary for playing Quake III, and a folder with no game in it is still not a game.

roots.purpose: load the base game and the mod being played

diagnostics.message: The client entered the map.
The engine could not find the map it was asked to load.
diagnostics.hint: Check that the PK3 you built is in the game directory this action names, and that the map inside it is at `maps/<name>.bsp`. Measured on ioquake3 1.36: the engine prints this, stays running and loads nothing.

diagnostics.message: The game's own player data was not found, so the client could not enter the map.
diagnostics.hint: Measured on ioquake3 1.36 with no `pak0.pk3`: the world loads and the client game then stops with `DEFAULT_MODEL (sarge) failed to register`. Quake III's client needs the player model that ships in the game you bought; a game folder without it can run a dedicated server and cannot run a client.

diagnostics.message: The engine is starting.
Quake III's own data was not found.
diagnostics.hint: The base game data root has to hold `baseq3` with your `pak0.pk3` in it. That file comes from a copy of the game you bought; Auto-Pigeon does not and cannot supply it.

diagnostics.message: ioquake3 found no Quake III game data and stopped.
diagnostics.hint: Measured on ioquake3 1.36: with no `pak0.pk3` in the base game data folder's `baseq3`, the engine prints this, names the folder it looked in and exits with status 3. `pak0.pk3` is id Software's and is yours to supply; the Companion ships none and downloads none.

diagnostics.message: The engine stopped with a fatal error.
diagnostics.hint: The engine's own last line is usually the whole diagnosis; read the job's log.

actions.title: Join a server
actions.description: Connects to a server somebody else is running. No `fs_game` is sent: a Quake III server tells the client which game directory it is running and the client switches to it.

actions.title: Host a game and play in it
actions.description: The client binary is a listen server as it stands: upstream documents `dedicated 0` — a server with a local player — as the client binary's own default, so this action does not send it. It sends the player limit, the port, and the two cvars that decide whether somebody who does not have your map can get it.

options.name: port
options.title: Port
options.description: `net_port`. 27960 is Quake III's own default; change it to run two servers on one machine.

options.name: pure
options.title: Pure server
options.description: Upstream: `sv_pure 1` restricts clients to the PK3s installed on the server; `sv_pure 0` lets them use their own. The values are the cvar's own.

values.title: Only the files this server has

options.name: allow_download
options.title: Send files to clients
options.description: `sv_allowDownload 1` lets a player who does not have your PK3 download it from the server. Without it they are refused and told what they are missing.

values.title: Let clients download what they are missing
